policy.canonical: The tested metric ingredients and instructions remain unchanged. Recipe JSON-LD uses those canonical fields; nutrition estimates remain unchanged.
policy.display: The site's existing US/Metric control selects paired ingredients and steps. Its US default and saved preference are reused.
policy.rounding: Volume equivalents are approximate, ingredient-specific and explicitly labeled. Original metric quantities are also retained in US text. Bulk meat, vegetables, ginger, cilantro and lime juice use weight ounces to avoid unreliable volume estimates.
policy.dividedIngredients: Honey, yogurt, oil, paprika, scallions and liquids retain their original splits. Where spoon rounding would distort a split, the measured total is divided by the original fraction.
policy.limitations: Brand, grind and packing affect volume. For the tested amounts, weigh the metric quantities. Weight ounces and fluid ounces are distinguished.

sources.use: Ounces rounded to one decimal for bulk ingredients and two decimals for small amounts; wrapper and pan dimensions use culinary rounding.

sources.basis: NIST lists approximately 4.9 mL per teaspoon, 15 mL per tablespoon and 237 mL per US cup. For consistency with this site's existing culinary convention, display equivalents round these to 5 mL, 15 mL and 240 mL respectively; all US equivalents are labeled approximate.
sources.use: Hot sauce, soy sauce, rice vinegar, water, coffee, maple syrup and vanilla. Original recipe already equates 30 mL maple syrup with 2 tablespoons and 5 mL vanilla with 1 teaspoon. No generic grams-to-cups conversion.
